Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

pity verb

also I pity you, feel sorry for, take pity on, have pity, feel pity for, show sympathy for, I feel sorry for, sympathy

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.1.72: miserēminī sociōrum (Lewis & Short s.v. misereō)
Traupman 105: I pity you, misereor tuī (pl. vestrī)
Traupman 156

misereor, miserērī, miseritus sum

verb, second conjugation, deponent, with the genitive: misereor tuī, I pity you

pity, feel sorry for

The person pitied is in the genitive, as after verbs of remembering: misereor tuī, vestrī.

Other words

  • miseret mē (+ gen.) — I feel sorry for

    impersonal, like taedet and paenitet: the one who feels it in the accusative, the object of pity in the genitive · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 4.5.1: ut nunc Menedēmī vicem miseret mē (Lewis & Short s.v. ut); Paul. ex Fest.: miseret mē is said like piget, paenitet, taedet (Lewis & Short s.v. misereō); Traupman 158

  • misericordia, misericordiae f. — pity, compassion

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.18: misericordia est aegritūdō ex miseriā alterius injūriā labōrantis (Lewis & Short); Traupman 156

  • commiserēscō, commiserēscere — to feel pity for

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 1.2.54 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 156

    (Lewis & Short: early Latin)

  • commiseror, commiserārī, commiserātus sum — to show sympathy for, bewail

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Traupman 158

    Lewis & Short: classical but rare.

Examples

  • Mē miseret aliōrum.

    I feel sorry for the others.Traupman 383

  • commiserēscere alicujus

    to feel pity for someoneTraupman 360

See also poor.
